channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Integrates into Global Market Through Economic Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan has transitioned from a closed, resource-based economy to a modern model integrating into the global market. Reforms like currency convertibility and tax liberalization have attracted foreign investment, particularly in green energy, textiles, and pharmaceuticals. Trade now spans over 160 countries, with key partners including China, Russia, Turkey, South Korea, and Central Asian nations.

item.title: Uzbek Startup Speko Launches on Product Hunt for Voice AI Solutions
item.description: Uzbek founder Beknazar Abdikamalov's startup, Speko, has launched on Product Hunt, addressing a key challenge in the global Voice AI market. Speko helps developers find optimal solutions for specific languages by integrating various providers through a single API, overcoming limitations of single-vendor systems.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan enhance cooperation on transboundary water resource protection
item.description: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan are strengthening collaboration on protecting and rationally using transboundary water resources, crucial for regional ecological stability and water security. A recent expert meeting, initiated by the UN ECE, focused on protecting the Tashkent transboundary aquifer and developing a partnership memorandum.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Electronic Entry Permit for Visa-Free Travelers
item.description: Starting August 25, Kazakhstan has implemented new legislation requiring an electronic entry permit for foreign citizens arriving from visa-free countries. The Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA), known as QazETA, will be processed through a digital platform. This new entry procedure was established by a law signed by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

item.title: Uzbekistan's SCO Summit Initiatives Focus on Security and Economic Connectivity
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev presented initiatives at the Bishkek SCO summit, emphasizing the organization's importance in Tashkent's foreign policy. The SCO is key for Uzbekistan to strengthen regional security, expand continental economic ties, and pursue an open, multi-vector foreign policy, as highlighted by the Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies.

item.title: New Specialized Boarding School Opens in Navoi for Talented Youth
item.description: A new specialized boarding school named after Al-Khwarizmi, with a capacity of 504 students, has opened in Navoi. The school aims to identify and nurture young talent, enhance scientific potential, and provide conditions for acquiring modern professions. The region reported a significant increase in students scoring maximum university entrance exam points.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reviews Progress on Nuclear Power Plant Construction and Satellite City Project
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed the construction progress of an integrated nuclear power plant and a satellite city in Jizzakh region. The project, crucial for energy security, has begun active construction, with significant excavation and concrete work completed. The total cost is $9.5 billion, with a goal to increase local product share to 30%.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Review 2026-2027 Budgets for Nuclear Power Project
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance will revise the 2026-2027 spending estimates for the "Uzatom" agency and the Directorate for the Construction of the Nuclear Power Plant. President Mirziyoyev instructed timely financing and avoiding delays in the project.

item.title: Xi Jinping Calls for New Middle East Security Architecture, Offers Maritime Security Cooperation
item.description: Xi Jinping urged the creation of a new security architecture for the Middle East and stated China's readiness to cooperate with regional states on maritime route security. This initiative gains importance due to disruptions in shipping through the Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab straits.

item.title: South Korean Police Suspect Four Uzbek Citizens of Supporting Terrorists
item.description: South Korean police have detained one and are investigating three other Uzbek citizens suspected of financing and supporting the Syrian-based organization 'Katiba al-Tawhid wal-Jihad' (KTJ). One suspect allegedly transferred cryptocurrency worth $4,600 to the group and purchased vehicles later sent to Syria.

item.title: UN Adopts Tajikistan's Initiative for International AI Day
item.description: The UN General Assembly has adopted a resolution initiated by Tajikistan, proclaiming August 31st as the International Day of Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence starting in 2027. This initiative builds on previous proposals and aims to foster global attention and cooperation on AI development and governance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes SCO Transformation into Geoeconomic Driver
item.description: At the SCO summit marking its 25th anniversary, Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented a vision for the organization's future, titled 'SCO-2040: Space of Common Development.' This initiative aims to transform the SCO into a powerful geoeconomic driver, facilitating investment, technology, and infrastructure projects.

item.title: UN Security Council to vote on Iran sanctions monitoring in September
item.description: The UN Security Council will vote in September on the monitoring of Iran sanctions, a move that could lead to confrontation with Russia and China. Both countries oppose the sanctions regime against Iran and the mechanisms overseeing its implementation.

item.title: IAEA notes Uzbekistan's nuclear infrastructure development but highlights unfinished issues
item.description: Uzbekistan has made significant progress in developing its nuclear energy infrastructure, but still needs to complete feasibility studies and strengthen its nuclear regulatory body, according to an IAEA mission. Officials reported high assessment of national nuclear infrastructure development to President Mirziyoyev.

item.title: Uzbekistan Implements New Data Management Model in National Statistics
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed results of the population and agricultural census, revealing preliminary figures of 39.047 million permanent residents. The census identified discrepancies in regional population data and clarified land boundaries, leading to a new data management model for national statistics.

item.title: International Financial Institutions Boost Green Energy in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing renewable energy as a key element of its green economic growth strategy, aligning with the 'Uzbekistan-2030' plan. The country aims to increase the share of renewables to 54% of electricity production by 2030, requiring enhanced cooperation with International Financial Institutions (IFIs).

item.title: Ukraine Warns ICAO of 'Unsafe Russian Airspace' Due to Drone Activity
item.description: Ukraine has officially warned the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) about the unsafe conditions in Russian airspace due to drone activity. Ukraine urges caution and calls for a ban on flights over Russia.

item.title: Turkey to Consider Full Membership in Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan stated that Turkey will consider full membership in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). He emphasized that this prospect does not entail severing ties with any other bloc or the West. Erdogan made these remarks after attending the SCO summit in Bishkek.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish 200-Hectare Industrial Zone for $9.5 Billion Nuclear Power Plant Construction
item.description: Uzbekistan will establish a 200-hectare industrial zone for the construction of a nuclear power plant valued at $9.5 billion. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed the project, which began active construction on June 4. The goal is to increase local product share to at least 30% and involve 7,000 local specialists.

item.title: Iran Urged to Reduce Gasoline Consumption Amidst Fuel Import Difficulties
item.description: Iranian citizens have been called upon to reduce gasoline consumption due to difficulties in importing fuel caused by a US sea blockade. Long queues have formed at gas stations in Tehran and other cities.

item.title: German Executive Partner Knauf Group Expresses Confidence in Uzbekistan's Industrial Potential
item.description: Uwe Knötzer, executive partner of Knauf Group, believes Uzbekistan's reforms and industrial modernization create opportunities for foreign investors. Knauf has operated in Uzbekistan since 1999, contributing to the building materials industry and professional education. The company currently manages three gypsum production facilities in the country.

item.title: Peru Declares State of Emergency in 893 Districts Due to El Niño Flood Risk
item.description: The Peruvian government has declared a state of emergency in 893 districts across 23 regions due to the risk of heavy rains and floods associated with El Niño. The emergency measures will last for 60 days, urging authorities to take preventive actions against landslides and floods.

item.title: Jizzakh NPP Project Mandated to Increase Local Content Share to at Least 30 Percent
item.description: The Jizzakh Nuclear Power Plant project has been instructed to increase the share of local products to at least 30 percent. The current share of local products is 21 percent, valued at $1.9 billion. National companies are also tasked with performing 65 percent of construction and installation work.

item.title: Himalayas Face Serious Risk of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods, UN Expert Warns
item.description: Millions in the Himalayan region face catastrophic risks from glacial lake outburst floods in the coming years, according to a UN assistant secretary-general. This warning follows a recent devastating glacier collapse in Nepal that caused over 1,000 deaths.

item.title: Pegasus Airlines reroutes Moscow-bound flights amid drone threat warnings
item.description: Turkish airline Pegasus Airlines rerouted several flights to Moscow back to their departure points. The airline also canceled dozens of flights between Turkey and Russia. This follows Ukrainian President Zelensky's warning about increased risks of flying over Russia due to potential drone activity.

item.title: Nuclear city to be built on 200 hectares in Jizzakh region
item.description: A city for nuclear specialists will be constructed on 200 hectares in Jizzakh. The project includes nearly 10,000 housing units, with 3,000 to be built in the first phase. The city will feature energy-efficient apartment buildings, schools, and kindergartens.

item.title: Ozon invites sellers to use warehouses in Kazakhstan for faster delivery
item.description: Online marketplace Ozon has offered sellers the option to store goods in its warehouses in Almaty and Astana, Kazakhstan. This aims to facilitate faster delivery to customers in Russia and boost sales within Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan due to quicker shipping times.

item.title: Chingiz Kaziev appointed Deputy Head of Jogorku Kenesh Apparatus
item.description: Chingiz Kaziev has been appointed Deputy Head of the Apparatus of the Jogorku Kenesh. Previously, Venera Kulataeva held this position and has now been appointed First Deputy Head of the Apparatus. The relevant orders were signed by the Speaker of the Parliament, Marlen Mamataliev.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Blocked Kloop.kg website hit by large-scale DDoS attack
item.description: The Kloop.kg website, blocked in Kyrgyzstan, was subjected to a powerful, multi-vector DDoS attack on August 31. The attack, aimed at making the site inaccessible, was recorded by Qurium, a foundation providing hosting services to Kloop.

item.title: World Nomad Games Feature Elechek Headdress Procession in Kyrchyn Gorge
item.description: A procession showcasing the traditional Kyrgyz women's headdress, the elechek, took place in Kyrchyn Gorge during the World Nomad Games. Participants displayed a large elechek made from 40 meters of fabric, measuring 80 cm long and 1.5 meters in diameter. The event aimed to promote Kyrgyz national heritage and women's role in culture.

item.title: Uzbekistan to conduct business registration survey from October 15 to November 30, 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan will conduct a business registration survey from October 15 to November 30, 2026, to enumerate all economic entities and update statistical registers. This initiative aims to address the significant shadow economy and improve competition by clarifying the status of registered businesses.

item.title: Dollar Exchange Rate Falls in Uzbekistan, Central Bank Announces September 3 Values
item.description: The dollar exchange rate has decreased in Uzbekistan. The Central Bank has announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective September 3rd. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Taxi Driver Charged 12,000 Som for Trip to Naryn, Failed to Complete Journey
item.description: Police in Karakol have located a taxi driver accused by a foreign tourist of overcharging and failing to complete a journey to Naryn. The 34-year-old driver, operating without a license, was fined 7,500 som, and his vehicle was impounded. The tourist had paid 12,000 som for the trip.

item.title: Air Arabia selected to transport pilgrims from Kyrgyzstan for Hajj 2027
item.description: Air Arabia will transport Kyrgyz pilgrims to Saudi Arabia for the 2027 Hajj, according to the Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Kyrgyzstan. The airline was chosen after a tender to carry 6,060 pilgrims.

item.title: Russia shortens medical examination period for labor migrants to 30 days
item.description: Russia has reduced the mandatory medical examination period for foreign citizens to 30 days from the previous 90 days after entry, effective September 1. The examination screens for dangerous infectious diseases, HIV, and drug use. Authorized medical organizations conduct the procedure, with results submitted electronically.

item.title: Uzbekistan President approves proposal for business registration event
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan has approved a proposal to conduct a business registration event. This event will take place from October 15 to November 30 and will involve surveying all economic entities operating in the country.

item.title: Tajikistan reviews investment project fund due to Middle East risks
item.description: Tajikistan is reviewing its investment project fund due to perceived risks in the Middle East. Further details on the specific projects or risks involved were not immediately available.

item.title: Iranian President's plane diverted to Rasht after SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The plane carrying Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian made an unscheduled landing in Rasht, Iran, instead of Tehran. The president was returning from Kyrgyzstan after attending the SCO summit. While flight data confirms the landing, the reason for the route change remains officially unexplained.

item.title: Uzbekistan may allow citizens to temporarily import foreign-registered cars
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to allow citizens to temporarily import foreign-registered cars for non-commercial purposes. A draft law is being developed by the Customs Committee and Ministry of Justice, due by December 2027. This measure aims to benefit Uzbek citizens working abroad.

item.title: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover reached $49.5 billion in seven months
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover for January-July 2026 reached $49.5 billion, an increase of $3.7 billion or 8.1% compared to the same period last year. Imports of machinery and transport equipment were $9.7 billion, while exports of goods, excluding gold, increased by 27.7%.
